text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- The Financial Markets Commission (CMVM) criticised banks for inducing clients to buy more shares than they can pay for outright at privatisation of state electricity company EDP - Electricidade de Portugal.

- Government has already received an 45 billion escudo offer to buy state airport authority - ANA (Aeroportos & Navegacao Aerea) from the Lusogare company, headed by a former ANA chairman Miguel Sarmento.

- European Commissioner for Competition Van Miert suspects the restructuring plan for state shipyard Lisnave may violate competition rules. The commissioner wants more details before taking a final decision in June.
- Portugal Telecom will not compete for a licence to operate in the mobile phone market in Brasil. Instead it will rely on its partnership with the Brazil's Telebras.

- Economy minister Augusto Mateus is trying to find a foreign investor to take over Grundig factory in Braga, northern Portugal. Projects being analised are supposed to create more jobs than those lost with the closing of the 'hi-fi' assembly line.
- According to a study by Barclays Bank, profits of state electricity company EDP - Electricidade de Portugal will grow at an annual average of 8.5 percent up to the year 2000.
